public_rationale: The contextual reading concerns overwhelming financial dependence, not the literal absence of other customers. Alphabet reports growing paid Gemini usage, which cautions against literal exclusivity but does not quantify the remaining revenue business. The reviewed records do not establish comparable AI revenue after excluding both labs' compute purchases at all three companies. 'Pathetic' supplies no separate objective threshold.
limitations: A literal reading of 'entirely' would produce a different test, despite the context acknowledging other revenue.
Usage, customer counts and model dependence cannot substitute for customer-level revenue.
The post does not define the financial importance of residual AI revenue.

from_speaker: Microsoft, Google, and Amazon’s AI revenues
our_interpretation: Treat 'without' as an accounting exclusion of the labs' direct compute purchases, not a forecast conditional on their disappearance.
Read 'entirely-dependent' as overwhelming practical revenue dependence. The surrounding discussion acknowledges other revenue, so a literal zero-other-revenue interpretation would be unfair.
The adjective 'pathetic' supplies no independent financial threshold and is not separately graded.

Use April–June 2026 as the latest comparable completed quarter before the post. The context also discusses Microsoft's completed fiscal year and calendar-year forecasts; those cannot be silently combined.
Payments by third-party customers for model access are distinct from compute spending by the labs, even when those customers use the labs' models.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable customer-level evidence shows that removing the labs' direct compute purchases leaves only a minor residual AI revenue business at each of the three companies.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence shows that one or more companies has a substantial independent AI revenue business after excluding the labs' direct compute purchases, sufficient to defeat the claim of overwhelming practical dependence.
